investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T23:58:31–34Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe's createAgent call was rejected before any agent was provisioned, so zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and all contract assertions went unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected the eval's POST /api/agents request with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval org has reached the swarm's per-org remote agent quota of 100, so no new agent can be created. Because agent creation is the first step in the runner branch (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1317: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)), all downstream evidence collection and contract assertions are skipped entirely. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a quota exhaustion condition in the production API against the eval org; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to indicate a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Eval org has accumulated 100 or more remote agents in the swarm backend (live or leaked/un-cleaned agents from prior eval runs), hitting the per-org quota limit enforced by POST /api/agents. The 409 body 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' is explicit.

SECONDARY — A prior eval run's withCleanup handler failed to delete a remote agent, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota. Repeated eval runs without successful cleanup would accumulate agents over time.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Terminated with GENERATION_NO_EVENTS Before Emitting generation_completed or Artifact URL
investigation.summary: The desktop-release image-generation-stream eval failed because the upstream SSE stream at /api/generate/image/stream emitted a generation_error frame with code GENERATION_NO_EVENTS before producing a generation_completed frame or an artifact URL, leaving both required evidence keys (frameTypes containing generation_completed, and imageUrlPresent=true) entirely absent. This is an eval-observed failure localized to the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint in the desktop-release runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The image generation backend terminated the SSE stream abnormally. After emitting two generation_start frames and eight generation_progress frames (all stuck at "Generating image..." with no advancing percent beyond 10%), the stream emitted a generation_error event with code GENERATION_NO_EVENTS and message "Image generation stopped sending progress before completing." The stream never emitted a generation_completed frame nor an artifact URL, so the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1430 could not populate the frameTypes or imageUrlPresent evidence fields required by the contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 269-272. The root cause is a mid-stream stall or timeout on the backend image generation pipeline serving /api/generate/image/stream, not an eval infrastructure misconfiguration.
proof: failed-check.evidence: The captured SSE frame sequence ends with event=generation_error, data.code=GENERATION_NO_EVENTS, data.message='Image generation stopped sending progress before completing. Try again in a moment.' No generation_completed frame appears anywhere in the 15-frame sequence.

failed-check.evidence: Only one generation_progress frame carries a percent field (percent=10); all subsequent progress frames omit percent entirely, indicating the backend stalled at an early stage and stopped advancing.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: Both frameTypes and imageUrlPresent are listed as missing required evidence, confirming neither assertion in the contract was satisfiable from the received frames.

expected-output.contract: Contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 269-272 requires frameTypes contains 'generation_completed' AND imageUrlPresent equals true; neither condition was met.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1409-1417: Runner calls apiSse against /api/generate/image/stream and at line 1430 writes evidence as { frameTypes: frames.map(f => f.event), imageUrlPresent: Boolean(imageUrl) }; because the stream never completed, imageUrl was never set and frameTypes never included generation_completed.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=120272 (approximately 2 minutes) shows the runner waited the full duration before the backend gave up, ruling out an immediate connection or auth failure.

sibling.image-generation-stream: The production-api sibling check failed with a different error (SESSION_OPEN_FAILED / 404 harness unreachable, latencyMs=2011), confirming the two failures have distinct root causes and are not a shared dependency failure; the desktop-release failure is specific to the image generation backend pipeline.
possibleCauses: Most likely — Backend image generation pipeline stall or upstream model timeout: The backend serving /api/generate/image/stream began generation (emitting generation_start and early generation_progress frames) but the underlying model call (gpt-image-2 or equivalent, per run-status-probes.mjs line 1418) stopped producing events before completion, triggering the GENERATION_NO_EVENTS watchdog. This is the most directly supported cause given the frame evidence.

Second — Upstream model provider rate-limit or quota exhaustion: The model provider may have throttled or rejected the generation request mid-stream after accepting it, causing the backend to stop receiving events and emit GENERATION_NO_EVENTS.

Third — Backend-side stream timeout or keepalive misconfiguration: A server-side idle timeout may have fired after the backend stopped receiving model events, causing the stream to be terminated with the GENERATION_NO_EVENTS error before the model finished.

Fourth (low confidence, not proven) — Regression introduced by commit e7b1227: This commit touched CI/workflow files and all three eval infrastructure files (features.json, check-expectations.json, run-status-probes.mjs) approximately 7 minutes before the eval ran. However, the commit's touched paths are CI/workflow files with no candidate code paths in the image generation backend, and the suspect-change confidence is rated low with only a weak metadata overlap on the term 'data'. This hypothesis is not supported by the frame evidence and should not be treated as causal without further inspection of the full diff.

investigation.summary: The production-api eval for image-generation-stream failed immediately (latencyMs=2011) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying HTTP 404, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner was not reachable at the time of the run. investigation.rootCause: The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1416) issued a request to /api/generate/image/stream and received a 404 response that was surfaced as SESSION_OPEN_FAILED. This means the agent runtime endpoint that backs image generation was not found at the configured harness URL (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL) at the time of the eval run. The root cause is uncertain between two possibilities: (1) the harness deployment targeted by the production-api runtime environment was down, misconfigured, or pointed at a wrong base URL, causing the 404 at session open; or (2) the /api/generate/image/stream route itself was removed, renamed, or became incompatible with the version the eval runner expects. The concurrent desktop-release failure (GENERATION_NO_EVENTS after 120s of progress frames) is a distinct failure mode and does not share the same error message, making a single shared dependency outage less likely than two independent degradations in the image generation pipeline.

investigations.summary: The desktop-release image-generation-stream eval failed because the upstream SSE stream at /api/generate/image/stream emitted a generation_error frame with code GENERATION_NO_EVENTS before producing a generation_completed frame or an artifact URL, leaving both required evidence keys (frameTypes containing generation_completed, and imageUrlPresent=true) entirely absent. This is an eval-observed failure localized to the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint in the desktop-release runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The image generation backend terminated the SSE stream abnormally. After emitting two generation_start frames and eight generation_progress frames (all stuck at "Generating image..." with no advancing percent beyond 10%), the stream emitted a generation_error event with code GENERATION_NO_EVENTS and message "Image generation stopped sending progress before completing." The stream never emitted a generation_completed frame nor an artifact URL, so the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1430 could not populate the frameTypes or imageUrlPresent evidence fields required by the contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 269-272. The root cause is a mid-stream stall or timeout on the backend image generation pipeline serving /api/generate/image/stream, not an eval infrastructure misconfiguration.
proof: failed-check.evidence: The captured SSE frame sequence ends with event=generation_error, data.code=GENERATION_NO_EVENTS, data.message='Image generation stopped sending progress before completing. Try again in a moment.' No generation_completed frame appears anywhere in the 15-frame sequence.

failed-check.evidence: Only one generation_progress frame carries a percent field (percent=10); all subsequent progress frames omit percent entirely, indicating the backend stalled at an early stage and stopped advancing.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: Both frameTypes and imageUrlPresent are listed as missing required evidence, confirming neither assertion in the contract was satisfiable from the received frames.

expected-output.contract: Contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 269-272 requires frameTypes contains 'generation_completed' AND imageUrlPresent equals true; neither condition was met.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1409-1417: Runner calls apiSse against /api/generate/image/stream and at line 1430 writes evidence as { frameTypes: frames.map(f => f.event), imageUrlPresent: Boolean(imageUrl) }; because the stream never completed, imageUrl was never set and frameTypes never included generation_completed.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=120272 (approximately 2 minutes) shows the runner waited the full duration before the backend gave up, ruling out an immediate connection or auth failure.

sibling.image-generation-stream: The production-api sibling check failed with a different error (SESSION_OPEN_FAILED / 404 harness unreachable, latencyMs=2011), confirming the two failures have distinct root causes and are not a shared dependency failure; the desktop-release failure is specific to the image generation backend pipeline.
possibleCauses: Most likely — Backend image generation pipeline stall or upstream model timeout: The backend serving /api/generate/image/stream began generation (emitting generation_start and early generation_progress frames) but the underlying model call (gpt-image-2 or equivalent, per run-status-probes.mjs line 1418) stopped producing events before completion, triggering the GENERATION_NO_EVENTS watchdog. This is the most directly supported cause given the frame evidence.

Second — Upstream model provider rate-limit or quota exhaustion: The model provider may have throttled or rejected the generation request mid-stream after accepting it, causing the backend to stop receiving events and emit GENERATION_NO_EVENTS.

Third — Backend-side stream timeout or keepalive misconfiguration: A server-side idle timeout may have fired after the backend stopped receiving model events, causing the stream to be terminated with the GENERATION_NO_EVENTS error before the model finished.

Fourth (low confidence, not proven) — Regression introduced by commit e7b1227: This commit touched CI/workflow files and all three eval infrastructure files (features.json, check-expectations.json, run-status-probes.mjs) approximately 7 minutes before the eval ran. However, the commit's touched paths are CI/workflow files with no candidate code paths in the image generation backend, and the suspect-change confidence is rated low with only a weak metadata overlap on the term 'data'. This hypothesis is not supported by the frame evidence and should not be treated as causal without further inspection of the full diff.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T23:58:31–34Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe's createAgent call was rejected before any agent was provisioned, so zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and all contract assertions went unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected the eval's POST /api/agents request with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval org has reached the swarm's per-org remote agent quota of 100, so no new agent can be created. Because agent creation is the first step in the runner branch (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1317: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)), all downstream evidence collection and contract assertions are skipped entirely. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a quota exhaustion condition in the production API against the eval org; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to indicate a broader production outage.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical 409 message, latencyMs=992, endedAt=2026-06-15T23:58:33.562Z — sibling check also failed at the same createAgent step.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical 409 message, latencyMs=961, endedAt=2026-06-15T23:58:34.524Z — all three remote-agents checks share the same upstream failure point.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting at createAgent before any evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:178-186: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the agent was never created.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1363 — the check completed in ~1.4 s, far below the 30 s warning threshold, consistent with an immediate API rejection rather than a timeout or slow provisioning failure.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Eval org has accumulated 100 or more remote agents in the swarm backend (live or leaked/un-cleaned agents from prior eval runs), hitting the per-org quota limit enforced by POST /api/agents. The 409 body 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' is explicit.

SECONDARY — A prior eval run's withCleanup handler failed to delete a remote agent, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota. Repeated eval runs without successful cleanup would accumulate agents over time.
TERTIARY — The eval org's quota was recently lowered by a backend configuration change, causing previously-acceptable agent counts to now exceed the limit.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit e7b1227 ('fix(observability): read desktop shares from api origin') touched all three implicated eval files (features.json, check-expectations.json, run-status-probes.mjs) approximately 9 minutes before the failure (committed 23:49:04, eval ran 23:58:31). However, e7b1227's touched paths are CI/workflow files with no matched needles for remote-agent logic, and the 409 error is a backend quota signal, not a runner code error. This commit is a low-confidence hypothesis with no supporting eval or source proof linking it to the quota failure.

investigations.summary: The production-api eval for image-generation-stream failed immediately (latencyMs=2011) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying HTTP 404, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner was not reachable at the time of the run. investigations.rootCause: The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1416) issued a request to /api/generate/image/stream and received a 404 response that was surfaced as SESSION_OPEN_FAILED. This means the agent runtime endpoint that backs image generation was not found at the configured harness URL (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL) at the time of the eval run. The root cause is uncertain between two possibilities: (1) the harness deployment targeted by the production-api runtime environment was down, misconfigured, or pointed at a wrong base URL, causing the 404 at session open; or (2) the /api/generate/image/stream route itself was removed, renamed, or became incompatible with the version the eval runner expects. The concurrent desktop-release failure (GENERATION_NO_EVENTS after 120s of progress frames) is a distinct failure mode and does not share the same error message, making a single shared dependency outage less likely than two independent degradations in the image generation pipeline.
